elements.title: Fallingwater (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the first owners of Fallingwater (pictured), a house in Pennsylvania, were rumored to hide tables when the house's architect visited?

elements.title: Rutherford Chang (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that in 2008, artist Rutherford Chang collected around 4,000 ink-dot portraits from The Wall Street Journal and reorganized them alphabetically into a yearbook-style publication?

elements.title: North Kent Mall (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that in 1997, several merchants of North Kent Mall in Grand Rapids, Michigan, did not know who owned the mall?

elements.title: Edward Cridge (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that in 1858, when 400 Black Americans experiencing discrimination in California resettled on Vancouver Island, clergyman Edward Cridge integrated Christ Church to welcome them?

elements.title: Georgia O'Keeffe's Hawaii series (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Georgia O'Keeffe's Hawaii series began as a commercial art commission for Dole pineapple juice?

elements.title: Mariel Molino (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Mariel Molino starred in the first Amazon original film for Mexico?

elements.title: a North Dakota TV station (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that the tower of a North Dakota TV station was the world's tallest man-made structure from 1963 to 1974 and again from 1991 to 2008?

elements.title: Tim Johnston (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that Tim Johnston pledged not to become a minister if he was elected to the House of Keys, but did so anyway?

elements.title: partnered up with evangelical churches (Wikipedia — did you know?)
elements.contents: ... that some drug trafficking factions in Brazil have partnered up with evangelical churches?
